sec:vortex-spectrum-intro:
The q-deformation of brane hydrodynamics forces vortex circulation onto a discrete ladder and pins helicity to a topological invariant. This section collects the modes produced by the braided monoidal structure and the conservation laws it enforces.

It opens with Remark: Vortex intensity modes: from classical fluids to q-deformation, which contrasts four classical mechanisms for discrete vortex spectra with the q-deformed mechanism to anchor the comparison. It then proves Proposition: Discrete vortex mode spectrum — the eigenvalues of the q-Laplacian on a filament are [k]_q^2 \cdot \hbar_q / L_q^2 — and interpret the resulting levels in Remark: Vortex intensity levels as fluid-dynamical orbitals. The central structural result is Proposition: Categorical helicity conservation: helicity operates as a topological invariant of the braided monoidal structure. Remark: Helicity as quantised topological charge reads this invariant as a discrete charge. It closes with Remark: Vortex reconnection as divisor surgery, establishing the birational picture of filament recombination. The subsequent section, Turbulence and acoustics, uses this to build the q-deformed energy cascade on tangles of these filaments.
rem:vortex-intensity-modes:
Remark Vortex intensity modes: from classical fluids to q-deformation. The substrate parameter q imposes an algebraic discreteness on vortex circulation absent in classical Navier--Stokes. Four classical mechanisms exhibit discrete modes but continuous intensity; the q-deformation closes this gap.

1. Kelvin waves on vortex filaments. A classical vortex filament supports standing-wave perturbations (Kelvin modes) at discrete wavelengths \lambda_k = L/k, for integers k \geq 1 and filament length L. The dispersion relation reads

  \omega_k =  \frac{\Gamma}{4\pi a^2}k^2
  \bigl(\ln(L/a) - \text{const}\bigr),

with vortex core radius a and circulation \Gamma. These modes are discrete in wave number, yet the circulation \Gamma remains a free continuous parameter. Under q-deformation, the filament inhabits the 1-jet bundle J^1 \mathcal{S}_n, and the q-Laplacian \Delta_q replaces the classical Laplacian. Its eigenvalues correspond to the q-integers [k]_q = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}), yielding a spectrum discrete in both wave number and intensity:

  \omega_k^{(q)} = 
  \frac{\Gamma_q}{4\pi a_q^2}[k]_q^2
  \bigl(\ln_q(L/a_q) - c_q\bigr).

As q \to 1, the q-integers collapse to classical integers, recovering the standard Kelvin spectrum.

2. Superfluid vortex quantisation. In superfluid helium and Bose--Einstein condensates, the macroscopic wave function \psi = |\psi|e^{i\varTheta} forces circulation to quantise as \Gamma_n = n \cdot h/m for n \in \mathbb{Z}. This constitutes a topological constraint: the phase must remain single-valued around any closed loop. The QOU analogue is the holonomy of the \mathrm{SU}(2) connection around a vortex filament. The primordial vortex carries topological charge because the representation theory of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) quantises the \mathrm{SU}(2) holonomy: the Casimir eigenvalue [j]_q[j+1]_q with j \in \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} replaces the continuous \Gamma.

3. Vortex breakdown states. In confined swirling flows (e.g., pipe flow), vortices transition between topologically distinct stable configurations — columnar, bubble breakdown, spiral breakdown — separated by finite energy barriers. These act as discrete states, not modes. In the brane fluid, the geodesic vortex fixed points of the q-deformed energy functional supply the analogous transitions: each fixed point forms a stable vortex configuration, and transitioning between them requires crossing an energy barrier set by q.

4. Stability eigenvalues. Smooth classical vortex profiles like the Lamb--Oseen vortex possess discrete eigenvalues in their linear stability spectrum. Perturbations grow or decay at specific discrete rates. For the q-deformed vortex, the weight-space decomposition of the adjoint bundle governs these eigenvalues. The longitudinal modes (Cartan subalgebra) govern the stable, decaying eigenvalues, while the ladder modes (E_\pm) govern the unstable, entangling eigenvalues. This separation is an algebraic consequence of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) structure, not an artefact of initial conditions.

The correspondence is mapped in Table: Classical fluid concepts and their q-deformed analogues.

prop:discrete-vortex-spectrum:
Proposition Discrete vortex mode spectrum. Let \varrho denote a stable vortex filament of length L in the brane fluid with substrate parameter q > 1. Let \Delta_q denote the q-Laplacian acting on sections of the normal bundle N_\varrho.

Then:

  1. The eigenvalues of \Delta_q restricted to \varrho form a discrete spectrum \{\lambda_k^{(q)}\}_{k \geq 1} scaling as

      \lambda_k^{(q)} = 
  [k]_q^2 \cdot \frac{\hbar_q}{L_q^2},

    where [k]_q = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}) is the q-integer and L_q is the q-deformed filament length.

  2. The spin label j \in \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) representation carried by the holonomy around \varrho indexes the intensity levels of the vortex. The vortex energy at level j equals

      E_j^{(q)} = 
  \frac{\hbar_q}{2I_q}[j]_q[j+1]_q,

    where I_q represents the q-deformed moment of inertia of the filament cross-section.

  3. The ladder modes E_\pm of the weight-space decomposition mediate transitions between intensity levels j \to j' under the strict selection rule |j - j'| = 1. The energy exchanged evaluates to

      \Delta E_{j \to j'} = 
  \frac{\hbar_q}{2I_q}
  \bigl([j']_q[j'+1]_q - [j]_q[j+1]_q\bigr).

  4. In the classical limit q \to 1:

    • [k]_q \to k, returning the classical Kelvin-wave spectrum.
    • [j]_q[j+1]_q \to j(j+1), reducing the energy levels to the rigid-rotor spectrum of standard angular momentum.
    • The selection rule \Delta j = \pm 1 reduces to the classical dipole selection rule.

prop:helicity-conservation:
Proposition Categorical helicity conservation. Let (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) be a QOU governed by brane fluid velocity v = \nabla_A S and vorticity \omega = \mathrm{curl}_Av = \nabla_A \times v. Define the categorical helicity of a vortex configuration \{\varrho_1, \ldots, \varrho_n\} as

  \mathcal{H}_q
  = 
  \sum_{i} \oint_{\varrho_i}
  v \cdot \omega\,ds
  + 
  2\sum_{i < j}
  \mathrm{lk}_q(\varrho_i, \varrho_j)
  \Gamma_i^{(q)}\Gamma_j^{(q)},

where \mathrm{lk}_q(\varrho_i, \varrho_j) specifies the q-deformed linking number and \Gamma_i^{(q)} = [j_i]_q[j_i + 1]_q indicates the quantised circulation of filament \varrho_i at intensity level j_i.

Then:

  1. Conservation. The quantum Euler equation strictly conserves \mathcal{H}_q: d\mathcal{H}_q/dt = 0.

  2. Decomposition. The categorical helicity resolves into three distinct topological invariants:

      \mathcal{H}_q
  = 
  \underbrace{\sum_i \mathrm{Wr}_q(\varrho_i)
    (\Gamma_i^{(q)})^2}_{\text{writhe}}
  + 
  \underbrace{\sum_i \mathrm{Tw}_q(\varrho_i)
    (\Gamma_i^{(q)})^2}_{\text{twist}}
  + 
  \underbrace{2\sum_{i<j}
    \mathrm{lk}_q(\varrho_i,\varrho_j)
    \Gamma_i^{(q)}\Gamma_j^{(q)}}_{\text{linking}},

    where \mathrm{Wr}_q and \mathrm{Tw}_q denote the q-deformed writhe and twist obeying the Călugăreanu--White--Fuller relation \mathrm{Wr}_q + \mathrm{Tw}_q = \mathrm{Lk}_q.

  3. Jones polynomial refinement. Classical helicity does not separate knot types. For a single thin tube of flux \Gamma it equals \Gamma^2(\mathrm{Wr} + \mathrm{Tw}) = \Gamma^2\,\mathrm{Lk}, the flux squared times the framing number [moffatt-ricca-helicity]. The value therefore depends on the framing of the tube, not on its knot type: it vanishes exactly for a zero-framed tube, and the unknot and the trefoil both admit zero-framed and non-zero-framed tubes. The Jones polynomial J_L(q) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_L)), computed via the Markov trace on the Iwahori--Hecke algebra, acts as a finer invariant. In the brane fluid, it evaluates to:

      J_L(q) =  \exp\!\Bigl(
    \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}
    \frac{1}{n}
    \mathrm{tr}\bigl((\check{R})^n\bigr)
    \cdot (q - q^{-1})^n
  \Bigr),

    capturing the full topological structure of the vortex tangle missed by \mathcal{H}_q.

    Where the closure enters, and what is conserved. J_L is a value of the tangle's braid word \beta only after the strands are closed: a cup below and a cap above each strand, the return arcs adding no crossing (closure). Closure is a trace, so it factors through the annular class of \beta in \mathrm{HH}_0 = H_n(q)/[H_n(q), H_n(q)], which keeps every sector character \chi_\lambda; the Markov trace then averages the sectors. Three statements follow directly from the stated input.

    • Isotopy. A smooth ideal flow carries vortex lines with it [moffatt1969], so the closed vortex link at time t is isotopic to the link at time 0. By the Alexander and Markov theorems [alexander1923, markov1936, birman1974] the two braid words are joined by conjugations, stabilisations x \mapsto x\,\sigma_n^{\pm 1} and their inverses. Along such a path the Markov trace changes only by the recorded stabilisation factors, so the normalised value J_L is conserved.
    • Fixed axis. If the tangle stays a closed braid on the same strands around a fixed axis, the path uses conjugations only. Then the whole annular class is conserved, and with it every sector character, which is finer than J_L. Under stabilisation the strand number changes and only the Markov-normalised value survives.
    • Reconnection. A reconnection replaces one crossing \sigma by \sigma^{-1} and breaks isotopy. By the skein relation \sigma - \sigma^{-1} = q - q^{-1}, every closure invariant jumps by exactly q - q^{-1} times its value on the word with that crossing smoothed.

    The two inputs to the isotopy statement, frozen-in vortex lines and Markov's theorem, are cited and not proved here. The classical counterpart of closing the strands is the asymptotic linking number, where long orbit segments are closed by short paths whose contribution vanishes in the limit [komendarczyk2008].

  4. Classical limit. As q \to 1, the representations collapse ([j]_q[j+1]_q \to j(j+1)), linking reduces to Gauss linking (\mathrm{lk}_q \to \mathrm{lk}), and \mathcal{H}_q simplifies to classical Moffatt helicity H = \int v \cdot \omega\,dV.

rem:helicity-physical:
Remark Helicity as quantised topological charge. The conservation of categorical helicity physically manifests topological charge conservation within the fluid. Under smooth inviscid (Euler) evolution, vortex lines are transported by the flow, so the evolution cannot alter the total helicity of a vortex configuration: helicity is preserved by every volume-preserving diffeomorphism, and it equals the average asymptotic linking number of pairs of trajectories [khesin2003, Thm. 2.2, Thm. 2.5]. It merely redistributes helicity among writhe, twist, and linking, as demonstrated by trefoil chirality flips. The statement does not extend to viscous flow. For Navier--Stokes with viscosity \nu > 0 the helicity H = \int v \cdot \omega\,dV obeys dH/dt = -2\nu \int \omega \cdot \mathrm{curl}\,\omega\,dV, which has no sign and does not vanish in general, and vortex lines of any knot or link type can reconnect while the solution stays smooth [enciso2017].

The exact quantisation of \Gamma_i^{(q)} = [j_i]_q[j_i+1]_q mandates that each term in the helicity sum remains individually quantised. Consequently, helicity is restricted to a discrete lattice structured by the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) representation labels \{j_i\}.

Two sources bound helicity by energy, and in both the bound is geometric, not topological. For a smooth field V on a compact domain \Omega of \mathbb{R}^3, S^3 or H^3, the Biot--Savart operator gives |H(V)| \le N(R)\,\|V\|^2, where N(R) depends only on the radius R of a ball with the volume of \Omega [deturck-gluck2008, §13, Thm. 7]. That note states it gives only a hint of the proofs in S^3 and H^3, so its constants are to be checked against the journal version before any use. When the pairwise linking numbers vanish, as for a Borromean configuration, the pairwise helicities H_{12} = \mathrm{lk}(L_1,L_2)\,\mathrm{Flux}(B_1)\,\mathrm{Flux}(B_2) are zero [komendarczyk2008, §6, eq. (6.1)], and the invariant that remains is the third-order helicity. On Borromean flux tubes it equals \bar\mu_{123}(L)\,\mathrm{Flux}(B_1)\,\mathrm{Flux}(B_2)\,\mathrm{Flux}(B_3) [komendarczyk2008, §6, eq. (6.6)], so it is cubic in the fluxes, not quadratic, and it is totally antisymmetric in the three components because \bar\mu_{123} is [komendarczyk2008, Rem. 2.3]. Its bound by the L^2-energy, |H_{123}(B;T)| \le C_T\,E_2(B)^{3/2}, has a constant set by the geometry of the invariant domain, and the source records that the estimate is meaningless once the handlebodies come close to one another [komendarczyk2008, §7, Thm. 7.1 and eqs. (7.6)--(7.7)]. The Freedman--He lower bound quoted there, eq.~(7.8), sums over components, each component taken against the whole link, and carries the pure constant (\pi/16)^{1/4} with no volume factor. These are statements about smooth fields; they bound the classical helicity and say nothing about the quantised labels \Gamma_i^{(q)}.
rem:vortex-reconnection:
Remark Vortex reconnection as divisor surgery. When two vortex filaments approach, the divisor \{\psi = 0\} undergoes surgery. In smooth inviscid (Euler) flow, vortex lines are transported by the flow and their link type is fixed, so a change of topology is incompatible with smoothness there. Viscous reconnection carries no such obstruction: there exist smooth solutions of the three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations in which vortex lines and vortex tubes of arbitrary knot and link type are created and destroyed in arbitrarily short time [enciso2017]. Reconnection by itself is therefore compatible with smooth classical viscous flow, and the role assigned here to the quantum pressure Q_q is to organise the surgery. Let D = \sum_i n_i\varrho_i denote the effective divisor framing the vortex configuration, where \varrho_i represent the filament components and n_i \in \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z} identify their intensity levels. Reconnection constitutes a birational transformation on the divisor:

  D =  \cdots + \varrho_i + \varrho_j + \cdots
  \quad\xrightarrow{\text{surgery}}\quad
  D' =  \cdots + \varrho_i' + \varrho_j' + \cdots,

where \varrho_i' and \varrho_j' designate the reconnected filaments. The surgery preserves three quantities:

  • Total circulation: \Gamma_i^{(q)} + \Gamma_j^{(q)} = \Gamma_{i'}^{(q)} + \Gamma_{j'}^{(q)} (enforcing conservation of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) Casimir).
  • Categorical helicity: \mathcal{H}_q[D] = \mathcal{H}_q[D'] (helicity conservation), although writhe and twist are free to redistribute. The redistribution is forced whenever the exchange acts as a crossing change between distinct filaments a \neq b of a pure braid. A crossing change of sign \epsilon = \pm 1 moves \mathrm{lk}(\varrho_a, \varrho_b) by exactly -\epsilon and the mutual helicity \sum_{a \neq b} \mathrm{lk}\,\Gamma_a\Gamma_b by exactly -2\epsilon\,\Gamma_a\Gamma_b, while the Reidemeister II and III moves leave both unchanged. Conservation of the total therefore requires an equal and opposite change in the writhe-plus-twist term, which is the transfer from linking to coiling observed in reconnecting vortex links [scheeler2014].
  • Total homology class: [D] = [D'] evaluated in H_1(\mathcal{S}).

Three types of divisor surgery.

Surgery type Divisor operation Physical process Hecke eigenvalue
Pass-through \varrho_i, \varrho_j \to \varrho_i, \varrho_j Elastic scattering q (symmetric)
Strand exchange \varrho_i, \varrho_j \to \varrho_i', \varrho_j' Reconnection -q^{-1} (antisymmetric)
Annihilation \varrho_i, \bar\varrho_i \to E_0 Pair annihilation \to exceptional divisor —

The first two classes map exactly to the two eigenvalues of the Hecke relation (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0, explicitly verifying the braid--fluid correspondence. The third class, annihilation, triggers when a filament encounters its orientation-reversed partner \bar\varrho_i. The pair physically collapses into an exceptional divisor E_0 \cong \mathbb{CP}^1, jettisoning energy 2\mathcal{E}_q[\varrho_i] as Kelvin-wave radiation along adjacent filaments.

Blowup and pair creation. The inverse mechanism — the blowup of an exceptional divisor — constitutes pair creation. When an intense Kelvin wave on a filament \varrho_k concentrates energy locally, and that density breaches 2\mathcal{E}_q[\varrho_{\min}] (twice the fundamental geodesic vortex energy), the exceptional divisor forcefully inflates into a filament--anti-filament pair:

  E_0  \to  \varrho_{\mathrm{new}} + \bar\varrho_{\mathrm{new}}.

These newly spawned filaments adopt the absolute minimum intensity level j = \frac{1}{2}. This serves as the precise fluid-dynamical mapping of pair production: a photon (the Kelvin wave) generates an electron--positron pair (the vortex--antivortex pair).

Selection rules. Reconnections are strictly filtered. The \mathrm{SU}_q(2) representation theory issues rigid fusion rules controlling divisor surgery. The specific reconnection \varrho_i + \varrho_j \to \varrho_{i'} + \varrho_{j'} proceeds if and only if the Clebsch--Gordan decomposition

  V_{j_i} \otimes V_{j_j}
  = 
  \bigoplus_{J = |j_i - j_j|}^{j_i + j_j} V_J

incorporates the target representation V_{j_{i'}} \otimes V_{j_{j'}} as a viable summand. This binds vortex reconnection entirely to the structural Clebsch--Gordan coefficients of the quantum group.

Connection to chirality. The trefoil chirality flip defines three avenues for chirality reversal. Translated to divisor terms:

  1. Passage through exceptional divisor: The vortex collapses briefly to E_0 and re-inflates bearing reversed orientation. This is effectively pair annihilation paired directly with opposite-chirality pair creation.
  2. Complex substrate rotation: The divisor sweeps through a homotopically non-trivial path mapped inside the complexified state bundle. No surgery occurs, but the ambient manifold must accommodate complexification.
  3. Reidemeister reconnection: A structural series of strand exchanges (Reidemeister moves) explicitly alters the core knot type. This denotes a shell transition, not a modification of particle identity.
sec:turbulence-acoustics-intro:
Having established the vortex spectrum and helicity invariant, this section examines collective behaviour: how discrete modes assemble into turbulent tangles and how perturbations propagate across the brane fluid as acoustic excitations.

It begins with Proposition: q-deformed energy cascade and modified Kolmogorov spectrum, which derives the inertial-range scaling of the energy spectrum E(k) as a function of q and the Planck--Reynolds number. Remark: Testable prediction: high-wavenumber deviations from Kolmogorov scaling extracts a falsifiable signature for BEC and superfluid experiments. Remark: Berry phase on the vortex moduli space calculates the geometric phase accumulated by filament configurations under adiabatic transport. Proposition: Kelvin wave dispersion from the q-Laplacian eigenvalue problem establishes the structural mechanics of vortex oscillations. Remark: Classical limit of the q-Kelvin dispersion verifies that the q \to 1 limit correctly recovers the classical self-induction law. Finally, Proposition: Acoustic horizon formation and gravitational emergence demonstrates that perturbations propagate on an acoustic metric whose horizons seed the analogue-gravity framework. The next section, Global regularity for q > 1, applies this identical spectral apparatus to control the nonlinear flow.
prop:q-turbulence-spectrum:
Proposition q-deformed energy cascade and modified Kolmogorov spectrum. In the brane fluid defined by substrate parameter q > 1 and Planck--Reynolds number \mathrm{Re}_q = 2/(q-1), the energy spectrum of a turbulent vortex tangle obeys a q-deformed Kolmogorov law.

  1. q-deformed energy spectrum. Let E(k) denote the energy per unit wavenumber. In the inertial range 1 \ll k \ll k_{\max}, where k_{\max} denotes the viscous cutoff imposed by \mathrm{Re}_q, the spectrum evaluates to

      E_q(k)
  = 
  C_q\varepsilon^{2/3}
  \frac{[k]_q^{-5/3}}{[k]_q / k},

    where \varepsilon represents the energy dissipation rate, C_q acts as a q-dependent Kolmogorov constant, and the ratio [k]_q / k corrects for the non-uniform spacing of q-integers. As q \to 1, [k]_q \to k and the spectrum converges to the classical Kolmogorov law E(k) = C_K\varepsilon^{2/3}k^{-5/3}.

  2. Discrete cascade. Classical turbulence cascades energy continuously from large to small scales. The q-deformed cascade operates discretely: energy transfers sequentially between modes indexed by q-integers [k]_q, executing at the transfer rate

      T_{k \to k+1}
  = 
  \varepsilon
  \frac{[k+1]_q^{2/3} - [k]_q^{2/3}}
       {[k+1]_q - [k]_q}.

    For large k, the denominator scales as [k+1]_q - [k]_q \sim q^k \cdot q/(q+1). The transfer rate thus drops exponentially at high wavenumbers, enforcing a strict structural UV cutoff.

  3. Finite cascade depth. The number of active modes participating in the cascade is bounded by

      N_{\mathrm{modes}}
   \leq 
  \bigl\lfloor \log_q(\mathrm{Re}_q^{3/4}) \bigr\rfloor
  = 
  \biggl\lfloor
    \frac{3}{4}
    \frac{\ln(2/(q-1))}{\ln q}
  \biggr\rfloor.

    The bound is the logarithmic form of the dissipation-scale cutoff q^{N_{\mathrm{modes}}} \leq \mathrm{Re}_q^{3/4} (every active mode lies below the Kolmogorov scale), which is the modeling hypothesis of the derivation; the passage from the cutoff to the stated bound is elementary. At the physical anchor q \approx 1.110, N_{\mathrm{modes}} \approx 21. (This accounts for all modes spanning the cascade; the Planck--Reynolds bound k_{\max} \approx 4 measures only those modes carrying significant amplitude.)

  4. Spectral gap. Below the fundamental mode k = 1, a spectral gap isolates the ground state (laminar flow) from the first excited mode:

      \Delta E_{\mathrm{gap}}
  = 
  C_q\varepsilon^{2/3}
  \bigl([1]_q^{-5/3} - [2]_q^{-5/3}\bigr)
   >  0.

    This gap halts the spontaneous onset of turbulence below a rigid threshold energy injection rate. The brane fluid remains structurally stable against infinitesimal perturbations, unlike classical Navier--Stokes where \mathrm{Re} \to \infty guarantees instability.
rem:q-turbulence-prediction:
Remark Testable prediction: high-wavenumber deviations from Kolmogorov scaling. The q-Kolmogorov spectrum collapses exactly to the standard k^{-5/3} law as q \to 1, ensuring compliance with all macro-scale turbulence measurements. At the Planck scale, however, the discrete cascade mandates high-wavenumber deviations from k^{-5/3} in BEC vortex tangles, perfectly tracking the q-integer spacing.

Observations of quantum turbulence in {}^{4}\mathrm{He} (Walmsley & Golov 2008) capture precisely these deviations. Convention attributes them to vortex reconnection, but the q-deformation of the energy cascade provides a rigorous structural origin.
rem:berry-vortex-moduli:
Remark Berry phase on the vortex moduli space. Fix an intensity level j and a topological knot type K. The moduli space \mathcal{M}_{j,K} classifies geodesic vortex configurations of type (j, K) modulo gauge equivalence:

  \mathcal{M}_{j,K}
  = 
  \bigl\{
    \varrho \colon S^1 \to \mathcal{S}
     \big| 
    \delta\mathcal{E}_q[\varrho] = 0,
    \mathrm{type}(\varrho) = K,
    \mathrm{level}(\varrho) = j
  \bigr\}
  \big/ \mathcal{G},

where \mathcal{G} denotes the gauge group. For the fundamental fermion (j = \frac{1}{2}, K = trefoil), \mathcal{M}_{1/2, T_{2,3}} forms a finite-dimensional manifold parametrised strictly by the position and orientation of the vortex filament.

Berry connection. The q-Schrödinger equation evaluated near the vortex ground state constructs a line bundle \mathcal{L} \to \mathcal{M}_{j,K}. The fibre over a vortex configuration \varrho corresponds to the ground-state eigenspace of the linearised Hamiltonian evaluated around \varrho. The Berry connection traversing this bundle reads

  \mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{Berry}}
  = 
  i\langle v_\varrho, d\, v_\varrho\rangle_F,

where v_\varrho denotes the ground state at configuration \varrho and d acts as the exterior derivative on \mathcal{M}_{j,K}.

Berry curvature. The curvature \mathcal{F} = d\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{Berry}} maps the local geometric phase per unit area across the moduli space. For a vortex configuration sustaining n well-separated filaments \{\varrho_1, \ldots, \varrho_n\}, the Berry curvature splits as

  \mathcal{F}
  = 
  \sum_i \mathcal{F}_i^{\mathrm{self}}
  + 
  \sum_{i < j}
  \mathcal{F}_{ij}^{\mathrm{mutual}}.

Here \mathcal{F}_i^{\mathrm{self}} derives strictly from the geometry of filament \varrho_i (the writhe contribution), while \mathcal{F}_{ij}^{\mathrm{mutual}} originates from the relative position of filaments \varrho_i and \varrho_j (the linking contribution).

Categorical interpretation. The braid--fluid correspondence maps the fundamental group \pi_1(\mathcal{M}_{j,K}) to a quotient of the braid group B_n. Traversing a closed loop in moduli space — enacting an adiabatic exchange of two vortex filaments — integrates the Berry phase

  \Phi_{\mathrm{Berry}}(\sigma_i)
  = 
  \arg\bigl(\text{eigenvalue of } \rho_n(\sigma_i)\bigr),

where \rho_n(\sigma_i) represents the braid-group representation acting on V^{\otimes n}. For the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) R-matrix, the two eigenvalues yield the distinct Berry phases

  \Phi_+  = \arg(q) = \frac{\pi}{\kappa}
  \quad(\text{symmetric channel}),
  \qquad
  \Phi_-  = \arg(-q^{-1}) = \pi - \frac{\pi}{\kappa}
  \quad(\text{antisymmetric channel}),

assuming q = e^{i\pi/\kappa} acts as a root of unity. The differential \Phi_+ - \Phi_- = 2\pi/\kappa - \pi yields the statistical angle — the exact phase distinguishing bosonic from fermionic exchange.

Connection to helicity. The total Berry phase accumulated by a vortex tangle L executing a closed loop in moduli space equals the categorical helicity \mathcal{H}_q of the tangle:

  \Phi_{\mathrm{Berry}}[L]
  = 
  2\pi\mathcal{H}_q[L] \pmod{2\pi}.

This equation maps helicity — a hydrodynamic invariant — directly to a quantum-mechanical phase, completing the structural triad:

  \text{Knot topology (Jones polynomial)}
  \longleftrightarrow
  \text{Fluid helicity}
  \longleftrightarrow
  \text{Berry phase (statistics)}.

  \partial_t^2 \eta
  = 
  \frac{\Gamma_q}{4\pi a_q^2}\Delta_q\eta
  -  \nu_q\Delta_q\partial_t \eta,

The q-Laplacian eigenvalue problem. The q-Laplacian evaluated on a circle of length L acts exclusively on L-periodic functions f(s). Its eigenvalue problem reads

  =  -\mu_kf_k,
  \qquad
  f_k(s + L) = f_k(s).

For the classical Laplacian (q = 1) in arc length s, the eigenfunctions are e^{2\pi i k s / L} with eigenvalues \mu_k = (2\pi k/L)^2. The derivation below works in the variable z = e^{2\pi i s / L}, where the eigenvalue is the dimensionless

  \mu_k^{(q)}
  = 
  [k]_q^2 .

The arc-length factor (2\pi/L)^2 is a change of unit, not part of the algebraic operator. All units are restored at once by the single factor \hbar_q / L_q^2 below. Derivation. The q-derivative operators define the q-Laplacian. Assign z = e^{2\pi i s / L} for a function f on the circle. Then:

  D_q f(z) = \frac{f(qz) - f(q^{-1}z)}{(q - q^{-1})z},

and \Delta_q = -zD_q \circ zD_q (composing the radial part of the q-Casimir). Operating on the monomial z^k yields

  = \frac{q^k z^k - q^{-k} z^k}{(q - q^{-1})z}
  = [k]_qz^{k-1}.

Consequently zD_q(z^k) = [k]_qz^k, proving

The exact eigenvalue reads \mu_k^{(q)} = [k]_q^2. Restoring physical units (filament length L_q and quantum of action \hbar_q) produces:

  =

  +  i\omega\nu_q\frac{[k]_q^2}{L_q^2}.

  =

  \frac{[k]_q}{L_q},

  \gamma_k^{(q)}

  \frac{\nu_q}{2}\frac{[k]_q^2}{L_q^2}

This is the quantum Peter--Weyl theorem, using Tannaka--Krein reconstruction (the fibre functor \tau gives A \cong \bigoplus_j \mathrm{End}(\tau(V_j)), spanned by matrix coefficients) and Schur's lemma.

Step 5: Compact resolvent. Given completeness, the resolvent (\lambda - \Delta_q)^{-1} acts on the eigenbasis as (\lambda - \Delta_q)^{-1}(z^k) = (\lambda + [k]_q^2)^{-1}z^k. Since [k]_q^2 \to \infty exponentially, the eigenvalues (\lambda + [k]_q^2)^{-1} \to 0 super-exponentially, so the resolvent is not only compact but trace-class:

  \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{1}{|\lambda + [k]_q^2|}
   \leq 
  \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{1}{[k]_q^2}
   \leq 
  \frac{(q - q^{-1})^2q^2}{q^2 - 1}
   <  \infty,

using [k]_q \geq q^{k-1}/(q - q^{-1}) for k \geq 1.

For v = \sum_k \hat{v}_kz^k with \lVert v \rVert_{H^1_q}^2 = \sum_k (1 + [k]_q^2)|\hat{v}_k|^2 < \infty:

   \leq 
  \sum_k |\hat{v}_k|
   \leq 
  \left(\sum_k \frac{1}{1+[k]_q^2}\right)^{1/2}
  \!\cdot\!
  \left(\sum_k (1+[k]_q^2)|\hat{v}_k|^2\right)^{1/2}

by Cauchy--Schwarz. The first factor is C_q (finite for q > 1 since [k]_q^{-2} = O(q^{-2k})); the second is \lVert v \rVert_{H^1_q}.

prop:q-ns-nonlinear-uniqueness:
Proposition Nonlinear estimates and uniqueness for the q-Navier--Stokes system. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) define a QOU anchored at substrate parameter q > 1. Let v represent a divergence-free solution to the q-NS system spanning initial energy E_0 = \lVert v_0 \rVert_A^2, and set C_q = (\sum_k [k]_q^{-2})^{1/2} as the categorical Sobolev constant.

(a) q-Ladyzhenskaya inequality. The advection operator B(v) = \mu \circ (v \otimes \nabla_q v) obeys

  \lVert B(v) \rVert_A
   \leq 
  C_q\lVert v \rVert_A\lVert d_q v \rVert_A.

(b) Enstrophy bound. The enstrophy \Omega(t) = \lVert d_q v(t) \rVert_A^2 satisfies

  \frac{d\Omega}{dt}
   \leq 
  \Lambda_q\Omega,
  \qquad
  \Lambda_q = \frac{C_q^2E_0}{\nu_q} - \nu_q  <  \infty.

In particular, \Omega(t) \leq \Omega(0)e^{\Lambda_q t} unconditionally for all t \geq 0, so the enstrophy remains finite at every finite time.

(c) Uniqueness. If v_1, v_2 represent two exact solutions with v_1(0) = v_2(0), then v_1(t) = v_2(t) uniformly for all t \geq 0.

rem:q-ns-proof-details:
Remark Proof details: nonlinear estimates, enstrophy evolution, and uniqueness. Proof of (a): q-Ladyzhenskaya inequality. In the eigenbasis v = \sum_k \hat{v}_k z^k, the advection is \widehat{B(v)}_m = \sum_{k+\ell=m} [k]_q \hat{v}_k \hat{v}_\ell. By Young's convolution inequality:

  \lVert B(v) \rVert_A
  \leq \lVert [k]_q \hat{v}_k \rVert_{\ell^2}
       \cdot \lVert \hat{v}_\ell \rVert_{\ell^1}
  = \lVert d_q v \rVert_A \cdot \lVert v \rVert_{\ell^1}.

Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the \ell^1 norm: \lVert \hat{v} \rVert_{\ell^1} \leq C_q \lVert v \rVert_{H^1_q}, giving the result.

Proof of (b): Enstrophy evolution. Differentiate \Omega = \sum_k [k]_q^2 |\hat{v}_k|^2 along the q-NS flow. The dissipation term is -2\nu_q \lVert \Delta_q v \rVert_A^2 with \lVert \Delta_q v \rVert_A^2 \geq \Omega. The stretching term is bounded by the q-Ladyzhenskaya inequality. Young's inequality ab \leq \varepsilon a^2 + b^2/(4\varepsilon) absorbs the stretching into the dissipation, leaving

  \frac{d\Omega}{dt}
  \leq -\nu_q\Omega + \frac{C_q^2 E_0}{\nu_q}\Omega
  = \Lambda_q\Omega.

Since \Lambda_q < \infty for q > 1, Gronwall gives at most exponential growth — no finite-time blowup.

At q = 1: \nu_1 = 0 and C_1 = \infty, so \Lambda_1 = +\infty. The bound gives no information.

Proof of (c): Uniqueness. Set w = v_1 - v_2. Energy method gives \frac{d}{dt}\lVert w \rVert_A^2 \leq 2C_q (\lVert v_1 \rVert_{H^1_q} + \lVert v_2 \rVert_{H^1_q}) \lVert w \rVert_A^2. Gronwall with w(0) = 0 gives w(t) = 0.

prop:core-levi-form:
Proposition The Levi datum of the vorticity plane field is the single scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi. Let D be the three-dimensional flow domain, \mathbb{R}^3 or \mathbb{T}^3 with the Euclidean metric. This is a statement on D, not on the state bundle \mathcal{S}: the chapter also uses \mathcal{S} as a surface, where a contact structure cannot exist. Let u be a smooth velocity field on D with vorticity \omega = \mathrm{curl}\,u, and on the open set D_\omega = \{\omega \neq 0\} let \xi = \omega/|\omega| be the vorticity direction. For a smooth scalar f > 0 on D_\omega set

  \varTheta := f\,\xi^\flat ,

where \xi^\flat is the metric dual of \xi. Then on D_\omega:

(a) The plane field is the orthogonal complement of the vorticity line: \ker \varTheta = \xi^\perp.

(b) \varTheta \wedge d\varTheta = f^2\,(\xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi)\,\mathrm{vol}. Hence \ker\varTheta is a contact structure at x if and only if (\xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi)(x) \neq 0, independently of f.

(c) The Levi datum of \ker\varTheta is one scalar. For v, w \in \xi^\perp,

  d\varTheta(v, w) = f\,(\xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi)\;\xi\cdot(v\times w),

so the restriction of d\varTheta to \ker\varTheta is f\,(\xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi) times the area form of the plane. There is no pair of Levi eigenvalues and no Levi condition number in dimension 3.

(d) \omega\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\omega = |\omega|^2\,(\xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi). The contact locus of \ker\varTheta is therefore \{\omega\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\omega \neq 0\}.

Proof. Part (a) is the definition, since f > 0.

For (b), d\varTheta = df\wedge\xi^\flat + f\,d\xi^\flat. The first term wedges to zero against \varTheta because \xi^\flat\wedge\xi^\flat = 0. The identity \xi^\flat\wedge d\xi^\flat = (\xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi)\,\mathrm{vol} then gives the formula, and f^2 > 0 gives the criterion.

For (c), df\wedge\xi^\flat vanishes on \xi^\perp, and d\xi^\flat(v,w) = \mathrm{curl}\,\xi\cdot(v\times w). For v, w \perp \xi the vector v\times w is parallel to the unit vector \xi, so \mathrm{curl}\,\xi\cdot(v\times w) = (\xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi)\,\xi\cdot(v\times w).

For (d), write \omega = |\omega|\,\xi. Then \mathrm{curl}\,\omega = |\omega|\,\mathrm{curl}\,\xi + \nabla|\omega|\times\xi, and \xi\cdot(\nabla|\omega|\times\xi) = 0. \square

Examples. For the Beltrami flow u = e^{-\nu t}(\sin z, \cos z, 0) on \mathbb{T}^3, \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi = 1 everywhere, so \ker\varTheta is contact on all of \mathbb{T}^3. For a straight anti-parallel vortex pair, \xi = \pm e_z is constant on each core, so \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi = 0 there and \ker\varTheta is integrable. This holds whatever the cross-sectional shape of the cores, so the core aspect ratio carries no Levi information.

Relation to the regularity criteria. The Constantin–Fefferman condition [constantin1993] and its \tfrac{1}{2}-Hölder improvement by Beirão da Veiga and Berselli [beiraodaveiga2002] bound the variation of the line field [\xi] on the high-vorticity set. Such a bound controls all of \nabla\xi, and so gives an upper bound on |\xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi|. The Levi scalar is one component of \nabla\xi. Neither its vanishing nor its non-vanishing implies either criterion.

Archimedean specialisation. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
conj:levi-degeneracy:
Conjecture Levi degeneracy conjecture: a vanishing Levi scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi on the high-vorticity set prevents blow-up. Setting. Let D be \mathbb{R}^3 or \mathbb{T}^3. This is the three-dimensional flow domain, not the state bundle \mathcal{S}, which the chapter also uses as a surface. Let u be a smooth solution of the unforced Navier--Stokes equations on D \times [0, T^\ast), with vorticity \omega and vorticity direction \xi = \omega/|\omega| where \omega \neq 0. Following The Levi datum of the vorticity plane field is the single scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi, the plane field is \ker\varTheta = \xi^\perp with \varTheta = f\,\xi^\flat, and its Levi datum is the scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi. For \Omega > 0 write H_\Omega(t) = \{x : |\omega(x, t)| > \Omega\} for the high-vorticity set.

Conjecture (Levi degeneracy, branch (B)). If for some \Omega > 0 the Levi scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi vanishes on H_\Omega(t) for every t < T^\ast, then u does not blow up at T^\ast.

Status of the conjecture. It is open, and no standard result supports it. The Constantin--Fefferman criterion [constantin1993] and its improvement by Beirão da Veiga and Berselli [beiraodaveiga2002] give regularity from coherence of the line field [\xi] on H_\Omega. That hypothesis bounds all of \nabla\xi from above. Vanishing of \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi fixes one component of \nabla\xi and does not imply it. Non-vanishing does not imply it either.

Branch (A) is withdrawn. The former branch (A) read "the Levi data stays bounded and non-degenerate at the collision, hence Navier--Stokes blows up". With \varTheta = f\,\xi^\flat this implication is false. On \mathbb{T}^3 take

  u(x, t) = e^{-\nu t}\,(\sin z,\ \cos z,\ 0).

Then \mathrm{curl}\,u = u, so \omega = u and \xi = (\sin z, \cos z, 0). The advection term (u\cdot\nabla)u = u_3\,\partial_z u vanishes, so with p \equiv 0 the field is an exact, global, smooth solution of the unforced equations. Its Levi scalar is \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi = 1 everywhere, so \ker\varTheta is a contact structure on all of \mathbb{T}^3, and |\omega| = e^{-\nu t} stays bounded. This refutes the implication under the reading \varTheta = f\,\xi^\flat, with the explicit solution as the invariant. It does not address any reading the chapter has not stated.

The growth exponent is withdrawn with it. The previous statement was a trichotomy on \beta = \limsup_\kappa \log\mathcal{C}_L(\kappa)/\log\kappa, where \mathcal{C}_L is the Levi condition number along a root-of-unity ladder q_\kappa \to 1. In dimension 3 the Levi form of a plane field is 1\times 1, so \mathcal{C}_L, \beta and the marginal window 0 < \beta < 1 are undefined.

What is true: a necessary condition for blow-up (standard, cited). Let u be a smooth solution of the unforced equations on D\times[0, T^\ast), in the class of [beiraodaveiga2002]. If u blows up at T^\ast, then for every \Omega > 0 and C \geq 0 there are t < T^\ast and x, y \in H_\Omega(t) with

  |\sin\angle(\xi(x, t), \xi(y, t))| > C\,|x - y|^{1/2}.

This is the contrapositive of the Beirão da Veiga--Berselli theorem. The Lipschitz form of Constantin--Fefferman follows a fortiori. In words, blow-up forces the vorticity line field to lose \tfrac{1}{2}-Hölder control on the high-vorticity set.

For a straight anti-parallel vortex pair the line field is constant, so this necessary condition fails and no blow-up occurs.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Generic categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
rem:core-levi-interpretation:
Remark Reading the Levi scalar: twist of the vortex lines, not core shape. The core Levi form reduces the Levi datum of the vorticity plane field \ker\varTheta = \xi^\perp to one scalar, \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi, where \xi = \omega/|\omega| is the vorticity direction on the three-dimensional flow domain. Its bearing on the Navier--Stokes problem is narrower than a single equivalence.

What the scalar measures. Where \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi \neq 0, neighbouring vortex lines twist about one another and \ker\varTheta is a contact structure. Where \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi = 0 on an open set, the planes orthogonal to the vortex lines are integrable there: locally the vortex lines are the normals of a family of surfaces. The scalar is a property of the line field [\xi], not of the cross-sectional shape of a vortex core. A straight anti-parallel pair has \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi = 0 for every core shape.

Withdrawn reading. This remark formerly displayed the chain "Navier--Stokes blows up if and only if the Levi form is non-degenerate at collision, if and only if the core aspect ratio \kappa(t) stays O(1)". Both equivalences are withdrawn; see Levi degeneracy conjecture. The first is the former branch (A). The smooth Beltrami solution u = e^{-\nu t}(\sin z, \cos z, 0) on \mathbb{T}^3 refutes it: its Levi scalar is 1 everywhere and its vorticity stays bounded. The second identified the core aspect ratio with a Levi condition number, which does not exist in dimension 3. The interpretation of each outcome, and the root-of-unity bound on the core aspect ratio read as a bound on Levi data, are withdrawn with them.

What survives. Two statements remain, of different status.

  1. Open. Branch (B) of Levi degeneracy conjecture: if \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi vanishes on the high-vorticity set, the solution does not blow up. No standard result supports it.
  2. Cited. The contrapositive of the Beirão da Veiga--Berselli criterion [beiraodaveiga2002]: blow-up forces the line field [\xi] to lose \tfrac{1}{2}-Hölder control on the high-vorticity set. Neither the vanishing nor the non-vanishing of \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi supplies that control, because the scalar is one component of \nabla\xi.

The contact-geometric question the chapter can still pose is therefore about twist of the vortex lines on the high-vorticity set, not about the shape of colliding cores.
def:ns-regular-qou:
Definition NS-regular quantum observable universe. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) define a quantum universe over a closed orientable spectral surface \mathcal{S} sustaining a brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} alongside quantum characteristic classes \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}).

The NS obstruction governing (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) is the global surface Euler class of the Reeb \mathrm{U}(1)-bundle \xi on \mathcal{S}:

  \mathrm{NS}(A)
  =
  \kappa_0
  =
  e(\xi)
   \in
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z},

whose degree is the Euler characteristic \deg e(\xi) = \mathrm{tr}(\kappa_0) = \chi(A) (QU-to-QOU, item 2).

Then (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) is classified as:

  • NS-regular if \mathrm{NS}(A) = 0 (equivalently \chi(A) = 0);
  • NS-singular if \mathrm{NS}(A) \neq 0 (equivalently \chi(A) \neq 0).

The NS obstruction tracks only the rigid categorical topology of (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) on \mathcal{S}. It operates independently of the selected substrate section q and ignores specific initial data:

\chi(A) \mathrm{NS}(A) = e(\xi) \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}) Internal model status
\neq 0 \neq 0 NS-singular (internal QOU label)
= 0 = 0 NS-regular (internal QPU label)

Why \mathrm{NS}(A) is defined on the global surface \mathcal{S} rather than on \Sigma. On any one-dimensional vortex-collision locus \Sigma \subset \mathcal{S}, sheaf cohomology vanishes in degree two (H^2(\Sigma, \cdot) = 0), so every surface class restricts to zero on \Sigma and \kappa_0|_\Sigma \in H^2(\Sigma, \mathcal{B}) vanishes identically for every \chi(A); in particular, Kummer non-divisibility on \mathcal{S} cannot infer a non-zero curve class from \chi(A) \neq 0. Defining \mathrm{NS}(A) as the global surface class e(\xi) \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}) yields a non-degenerate topological invariant determined directly by \deg e(\xi) = \chi(A), whereas \mathrm{NS}(A) does not localise on a collision curve \Sigma.

The defining observability axiom \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 acts as a sufficient condition guaranteeing \chi(A) \neq 0 (forcing rigid irreducibility on the adjoint representation to guarantee a nonzero Euler class). Consequently every quantum observable universe satisfies \mathrm{NS}(A) = e(\xi) \neq 0 and is internally NS-singular; a \chi(A) = 0 universe is a quantum pre-universe (QPU), not a QOU.

Scope of the 3D Navier--Stokes bridge (framework model correspondence). "NS-regular" and "NS-singular" are internal categorical labels for the global Euler class \mathrm{NS}(A) = e(\xi) on \mathcal{S}. Connecting this internal invariant to global regularity or finite-time blowup of the classical unforced 3D incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on \mathbb{R}^3 or \mathbb{T}^3 is a framework model correspondence, not a deductive PDE equivalence:

  1. Tao's averaged Navier--Stokes barrier. By Tao's theorem (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 29 (2016), 601--674), any regularity argument for critical or supercritical 3D Navier--Stokes whose inputs are invariant under rotational, dilation, and Fourier-multiplier averaging of the bilinear advection operator B(u, u) = P[(u \cdot \nabla)u] applies unchanged to an averaged operator \tilde{B}(u, u) that admits finite-time blowup. Because \mathrm{NS}(A) = e(\xi) is a purely topological invariant of \mathcal{S} using no property of the PDE nonlinearity B, the condition \mathrm{NS}(A) = 0 cannot by itself constitute a deductive proof of classical 3D global regularity.
  2. Scaling branch at q \to 1. Taking q \to 1 at fixed \nu_q = (q - 1)/(2q) yields the inviscid Euler limit (\nu_1 = 0); viscous Navier--Stokes sits on the fixed-\hbar_q scaling branch, and transferring internal q > 1 subcritical regularity or q \to 1 surface obstructions across that limit to 3D physical solutions remains an open bridge.

rem:observability-fluid-context:
Remark Observability for the brane fluid. Before defining NS regularity, the QOU observability axiom \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 is clarified structurally within the fluid-dynamical setting.

Categorical statement. No morphism \phi \colon \mathbf{1} \to \mathrm{Ad}(A) exists within \mathbf{C}. The adjoint representation of the Frobenius--Hopf object A admits no trivial sub-object.

Gauge-theoretic translation. H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) = 0: no nonzero section of the adjoint bundle \mathrm{Ad}(P) = P \times_G \mathfrak{g} remains gauge-equivariant. Every infinitesimal gauge transformation operates nontrivially against some observable.

No contact-geometric translation. Observability does not translate into everywhere non-degeneracy of a Levi form \mathcal{L}_\varTheta: on the three-dimensional flow domain the plane field \ker\varTheta = \xi^\perp perpendicular to the vorticity direction \xi has Levi datum given by the single scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi (core Levi form), and no result in this chapter links the non-vanishing of that scalar to \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0.

Fluid-dynamical translation. Evaluated on the brane fluid:

  1. No stagnant directions. Every spatial direction in the brane actively drives fluid dynamics. The gauge structure strictly forbids directions supporting an identically zero velocity field.
  2. No hidden laminar sectors. If \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) \neq 0, a gauge symmetry would render a designated direction dynamically trivial, yielding a guaranteed laminar sector. Observability precludes this: every direction forces dynamic engagement.
  3. Vortex stretching is isotropic. The weight-space decomposition of the adjoint bundle lacks a trivial component. Consequently, the stretching term (\omega \cdot \nabla)v applies pressure in all directions. Vorticity cannot vent into a "neutral" axis.

The alternative: what \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) \neq 0 implies.

A surviving morphism \phi \colon \mathbf{1} \to \mathrm{Ad}(A) would establish a preferred direction operating in the brane:

  • A designated axis where vortex stretching zeroes out.
  • A physical channel permitting vorticity to drain without local concentration.

This structural leak would provide a persistent regularity mechanism: vorticity would dissipate cleanly along the preferred direction rather than concentrating into a blowup.

Observability asserts that no such escape route exists. The brane fluid remains dynamically active; colliding vortices lack any structural geometry to dissipate through.
